question.text: An investment promises the following cash flows: Rs. 10,000 at end of Year 1, Rs. 15,000 at end of Year 2, and Rs. 20,000 at end of Year 3. At a discount rate of 8%, the present value of these cash flows is closest to:

explanation.text: The Logic: PV = 10,000/(1.08)^1 + 15,000/(1.08)^2 + 20,000/(1.08)^3 = 9,259 + 12,860 + 15,877 = approximately Rs. 37,996 (about Rs. 38,000). Among the listed options, Rs. 38,642 is the closest value. The Trap: Rs. 45,000 is the simple sum without discounting. Always discount future cash flows to find their present value. Note: The calculation rounds to about Rs. 37,996; the keyed option Rs. 38,642 is selected as the closest of the available choices, not because it is the precise computed value.
